title: Reading the Field
logline: Across one growing season, a farmer in a tank-irrigated village makes dozens of small calls, when to flood, when to weed, when to hold water back, none of them written down, all of them adding up to a harvest.
human_question: What does it mean to know something so well that you can act on it instantly, without stopping to think it through?

premise.story: One paddy season, from sowing to harvest, following a farmer's daily, practical decisions and their outcome.
premise.place: A tank-irrigated rice village in the dry zone.
premise.experience: The unglamorous, high-stakes skill of reading a field, a sky and a season, and getting it right or wrong.

concept_links.why: The source separates recognising a thing, noticing more about it, and understanding it so well that the understanding itself can act; it names exactly this practical skill, seeing what makes things grow and what makes them decline, and knowing on the spot what serves wellbeing [C096-P4:L30; C096-P4:L66–L72]. The farmer's field skill is an echo of that practical strand, not a claim about the farmer's inner life.
This kind of seeing is placed, in the larger map, only after conduct and a settled mind; the film does not need to say this, but the farmer's steady, repeated attention can carry the idea.

what_camera_could_observe: Walking the bunds at dawn, checking water levels and plant colour
A quick decision made after sudden rain or a pest sighting
Conversations with neighbours about what went wrong or right last season
The harvest itself, good or bad, and the farmer's own account of the season's calls
what_must_be_real: The farmer's actual land, water rights, and economic stakes. Market prices, weather and yield are not adjusted for the story.

possible_arc.opening: Water released into the field for the first time this season.
possible_arc.turn: A decision made under pressure, right or wrong.

requirements: A farming household willing to be followed across a full season
Access to the field and irrigation system
Patience for a long shooting schedule tied to the crop calendar

suggestions.name: A tank-irrigated paddy village
suggestions.season_notes: Tied to the Yala or Maha growing season
suggestions.verify: A specific willing household must be identified.

risks: Reducing a farmer's knowledge to a doctrinal illustration
A bad season could read as the farmer's fault when climate and market forces are the real cause
drop_if: No household will commit to a full-season shoot, or a crop failure would make filming exploitative

connections.note: From settling the mind to the further work of seeing clearly, which this idea follows into ordinary working wisdom.
The same season's harvest, taken stock of, flows into the following idea's image of crossing and letting go.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
